public_answer: Opening position from QA Reviewer C: Rank 1 — CSRF, severity High. The password-change endpoint at L009 performs a state-changing action via GET-style parameters with no anti-CSRF token visible in the packet. The only protection is the referer check at L010, which uses `stripos($_SERVER['HTTP_REFERER'], $_SERVER['SERVER_NAME'])` — a substring match that accepts any referer containing the server name anywhere in the string, and is trivially satisfied by any request originating from a page on the same host. L007 confirms that requests triggered from the vulnerable `/displayname` page carry `Referer: http://webapp/displayname`, which would pass the L010 check. Rank 2 — XSS_Reflected, severity Medium. Directly evidenced at L001–L006 (parameter reflected, payload `` executes on load). Rank 3 — NoFinding for any other class; nothing else in the packet supports additional labels. The user assumption is wrong: the referer check at L010 is a substring match and does not reliably ensure intra-application origin, so the password-change functionality is not safe.
